conventions.convention: Particle positions have length dimension, frame time has duration dimension, masses are fixed and positive, and the mass operator is block diagonal with blocks m_i I_3. Constraint components carry separately declared dimensions.

The basic holonomic datum permits C² G and requires spatial rank k only on its nonempty zero locus. The multiplier-flow theorem separately requires C³ G, spatial rank k everywhere on O, and C¹ F; its force-dependent functions are defined on O′ = O ∩ (I₀ × Q).
Virtual displacements are ker D_xG at frozen time. Permitted velocities satisfy G_t + D_xG v = 0. Consistent initial data satisfy both G = 0 and this velocity condition.
Scleronomic means the zero locus is a condition on x alone within O; rheonomic means otherwise. Scleronomicity implies G_t = 0 on the locus, but the converse is explicitly not asserted.
The ideal reaction has sign R = D_xGᵀ λ, so its actual power is R·x′ = −λ·G_t. Zero virtual work does not imply zero actual work.

Moving coordinates satisfy x = R(t)y + c(t), with unchanged time. Angular velocity uses the body convention Ω = RᵀR′ and Ωz = ω × z; spatial angular velocity is Rω. All four inertial terms enter with minus signs.
The inertial-chart criterion quantifies over every time, position and velocity in I × R³ × R³, rather than just the data along one motion.

Velocity constraints are affine laws Av + b = 0 with C² coefficients and full row rank. Chetaev virtual displacements are ker A. Local holonomic equivalence requires A = ρΦ_x and b = ρΦ_t with invertible ρ; failure of a global factorization alone does not establish local nonholonomicity.

The rolling example declares a separate reduced two-coordinate model, with x length-valued, θ dimensionless, M = diag(m,I), and generalized force components having force and torque dimensions. Its static-contact capacity law is an adopted model assumption.

load_bearing.statement: A holonomic datum has open nonempty O, 1 ≤ k ≤ 3N−1, C² G, nonempty Σ = {G = 0} contained in I₀ × Q, and rank-k D_xG on Σ. Constrained motions satisfy Mx″ = F(t,x,x′) + R. Virtual displacements are ker D_xG; permitted velocities satisfy G_t + D_xG v = 0. Scleronomicity is time-independence of the locus within O.

Along every constrained motion the reaction satisfies R(t)·δ = 0 for every δ ∈ ker D_xG(t,x(t)); equivalently, at each time there is a unique λ(t) with R(t) = D_xG(t,x(t))ᵀλ(t). The ideality condition is an adopted physical restriction, not a consequence of imposing the constraint.

Under the adopted holonomic model and ideal-reaction law, C³ G with full spatial rank throughout O and C¹ F determine the unique multiplier and explicit acceleration on O′ × R^{3N}. Ideal constrained motions are exactly first-order-system solutions with consistent data; each consistent datum has a unique maximal solution, the constraint and its differentiated form are preserved, and R·x′ = −λ·G_t.
A moving spatial chart is specified by a nondegenerate interval I and C² maps c:I→R³ and R:I→SO(3), with x = Ry + c, Ω = RᵀR′, Ωz = ω × z, and inertial field −(2ω × y′ + ω′ × y + ω × (ω × y) + Rᵀc″).

With the multiplier theorem's regularity and rank hypotheses and a C² potential presentation F_i = −∇_{x_i}U + d_i, E′ = ∂_tU + Σ_i d_i(t,x,x′)·x_i′ − λ·G_t. Scleronomic constraints have zero reaction power; a static potential and vanishing evaluated residual forces then suffice for conservation. The integrated work identity holds on every closed motion subinterval.

Along each force-model motion, m_i y_i″ = RᵀF_i + m_iτ. The inertial field τ vanishes on all I × R³ × R³ if and only if R is constant and c is affine on I; precisely then the moving chart restricts an inertial adapted chart with zero time shift.

The velocity-constraint branch adopts Av + b = 0 and the d'Alembert reaction R annihilating ker A, equivalently R = Aᵀμ with unique μ. Holonomic equivalence is the stated invertible factorization through derivatives of Φ; locally nonholonomic means no such factorization exists on any neighborhood of the specified point.

concerns.concern: Definition (a) permits G of class C² but concludes that each nonempty Σ_t is an embedded submanifold by thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold. That supplier requires a smooth map, and def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart requires smooth slice charts. The asserted smooth conclusion need not hold: for N=1, k=1, G(t,x)=x₂−|x₁|³ has rank-one spatial derivative everywhere and is C², but its zero locus is not a smooth embedded surface at x₁=0. A finite-regularity supplier/convention or stronger hypothesis is needed.

Clause (iv).4 excludes 'active mechanisms that drive the constraint (motors, moving walls driven by external equipment)' and requires their driving to be an additional force contribution. The rotating-wire example instead prescribes rotation, omits driving details, and assigns the resulting injected power entirely to the ideal reaction. Clarify whether this exclusion concerns a direct applied drive on the modeled particle or also a prescribed driven support; the present wording makes the example's applicability to this postulate unclear.

Clause (e) says the supplier proves that 'the unique d'Alembert motion is not vakonomic'. The supplier proves uniqueness of the maximal motion and expressly says other motions through the datum are its restrictions. Since this definition permits differing motion intervals, there is not literally one motion as a domain-bearing function. State maximal uniqueness or uniqueness up to restriction.

The 'What is proved' section repeats 'the unique d'Alembert motion' without the maximal/restriction qualification supplied by cex-cm-dalembert-and-vakonomic-evolutions-differ, steps 2.1–3.1. The subsequent solution-set non-inclusion is sound; the uniqueness wording needs qualification.

F1 attributes the explicit first-order-system equivalence to a 'C² regular constraint' without the chart proposition's C³ constraint and C¹ force hypotheses. prop-cm-ideal-holonomic-system-in-a-time-dependent-chart states those stronger hypotheses. The actual affine constraint and constant applied force satisfy them, so the calculation is sound, but the quoted supplier assertion is stronger than its source.

F4 says G(q(t))=0 is equivalent to x′−aθ′=0 and to x−aθ being constant. The latter conditions only preserve an arbitrary constant; they require an initial condition G(q(t₀))=0 to imply the chosen zero-level constraint. For example q(t)=(1,0) has zero velocity and constant x−aθ=1 but does not satisfy G=0. The main M1 model explicitly imposes G=0, but this Facts assertion needs the missing initial-level qualification.

Clause 2 quantifies over any constrained motion, while Verification steps 1.2 and 2.2 work with a motion already presented as x=X(θ). The existence of a C² real angular lift on its interval is not established. This can be supplied directly by integrating angular velocity after choosing one initial angle, but it is an omitted bridge for the universal claim.

alerts.finding: Definition (f) assumes U is C² and concludes 'U⁻¹(c) is an embedded submanifold' using thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold and def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart. Those sources require smooth maps and smooth slice charts. U(x)=x₂−|x₁|³ has nonvanishing gradient and is C² but its zero-level graph is not smooth at x₁=0. This is the same finite-regularity mismatch encountered in the owned holonomic definition.

The Statement ends 'Equivalently, the row vector of ℓ is Aᵀλ.' For A:R^m→R^n, Aᵀλ is an m×1 column, whereas the row representing ℓ is 1×m. The proved scalar identity is correct; the final equivalent formulation should use the column representing ℓ or the row λᵀA.

Definition (c) says 'the state curve z=(x,x′):J→D', but (a) defines D⊂R×R^{6N} as the time-state domain. The pair z has only 6N coordinates; it is the graph t↦(t,z(t)) that lies in D. The same typing recurs in the explanatory equivalence. The equation and uniqueness argument remain recognizable.

seams_checked.note: The multiplier-flow theorem carries C³ G, full rank throughout the ambient domain and C¹ F when applying the chart proposition. The nonholonomic comparison uses the specified counterexample and proves only the stated non-inclusion.
Kinetic and mechanical energy definitions and the potential-plus-residual presentation are retained; reaction power is added explicitly rather than attributed to the unconstrained force map.
The constrained branch is explicitly separate from the unconstrained Newtonian equation. Moving-chart covariance uses block rotations and repeated translations/boosts on the transferred domain.
Fixed positive masses, SI dimensions, inertial adapted charts and coordinate derivatives are used with their declared meanings. The owned C²-to-smooth-locus concern is recorded separately.
The work-energy supplier is applied to total non-potential force d+R, with the potential defined on an open time neighborhood of every motion subinterval.
The acceleration identity is used for C² chart and motion data with x=Ry+c and Ω=RᵀR′. The inertial-chart construction matches adapted affine geometry.
The skew-matrix correspondence and conjugation law give the stated body/spatial angular-velocity conversion with compatible signs.
The bead, pendulum and moving-chart examples declare constant force maps with the required regularity. The rolling reduction is explicitly a separate declared model.
Mass, position, angular, force, torque and energy dimensions are explicitly declared; numerical inputs remain model data rather than measurements.

Rolling F1 restates the chart-flow result under C² rather than C³ constraints and omits its C¹ force hypothesis. Rolling F4 also omits the initial zero-level condition when equating the velocity law with G=0. Both concerns are recorded on the owned example; its actual affine data support the calculations.
The bead uses U=mgz and the pendulum U=mgy; kinetic energies, reaction powers and explicit model-value energy calculations agree with these presentations.
The rotating-chart example respects x=Ry+c and the body convention, and its four terms at t=0 sum to −3e₁−e₂ as claimed.

The generalized-coordinate definition and reduction theorem use the scleronomic locus, the frozen kernel, the adopted ideal law and unique residual reaction. They add an explicit C³ immersed parametrization and its coverage/domain conditions.

The pendulum elimination example uses rank on the locus, as the basic definition allows, and the ideal reaction law. Its reduction does not invoke the multiplier-flow theorem's stronger all-ambient rank hypothesis.
The heavy-top postulate explicitly adopts an analogous continuum pivot idealization and zero pivot torque; it does not claim that the particle postulate alone proves the continuum law.
Hamilton equivalence clause 4 restricts to scleronomic regular constraint parametrizations with ideal reactions and no residual forces, using the established elimination theorem.
The pendulum Legendre example uses smooth circle constraints and local angular charts, retains the ideal-reaction assumption and declares the distinct multiplier dimensions.
